name: Security Audit

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 6 * * 1" # Every Monday at 06:00 UTC
  push:
    paths:
      - "**/Cargo.toml"
      - "**/Cargo.lock"
      - "deny.toml"
  pull_request:
    paths:
      - "**/Cargo.toml"
      - "**/Cargo.lock"
      - "deny.toml"

jobs:
  audit:
    name: Dependency Audit
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install cargo-audit
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-audit

      # Ignored advisories, each with a justification:
      #   RUSTSEC-2025-0141 bincode      -- dev-dependency, unmaintained, no upgrade path
      #   RUSTSEC-2025-0057 fxhash       -- transitive dependency, unmaintained
      #   RUSTSEC-2024-0384 instant      -- transitive dependency, unmaintained
      #   RUSTSEC-2026-0235 rkyv 0.7.46  -- NOT in any build graph. rkyv is an
      #     optional dependency of rust_decimal (via byte-unit, itself a
      #     dev-dependency of shodh-redb-bench) that no feature in this
      #     workspace enables. It appears only in Cargo.lock, which is
      #     feature-agnostic, and cargo-audit scans the lockfile without
      #     resolving features. Verified never compiled:
      #       cargo tree -i rkyv --workspace --all-features --target all
      #     prints "nothing to print", and `cargo tree -p byte-unit -e features`
      #     shows rust_decimal pulling only arrayvec and num-traits.
      #     cargo-deny, which is feature-aware, does not flag it.
      #     Re-evaluate if anything ever enables rust_decimal's `rkyv` feature.
      - name: Run cargo-audit
        run: cargo audit --ignore RUSTSEC-2025-0141 --ignore RUSTSEC-2025-0057 --ignore RUSTSEC-2024-0384 --ignore RUSTSEC-2026-0235

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny@0.19.0

      - name: Check advisories
        run: cargo deny check advisories

      - name: Check licenses
        run: cargo deny --workspace --all-features check licenses

      - name: Check bans
        run: cargo deny --workspace check bans

      - name: Check sources
        run: cargo deny --workspace check sources

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches:
      - master

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Fast checks: format, clippy, deny (runs first)
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  lint:
    name: Lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      RUSTFLAGS: --deny warnings
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/bin/
            ~/.cargo/registry/index/
            ~/.cargo/registry/cache/
            ~/.cargo/git/db/
            target/
          key: lint-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.toml', '**/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: lint-

      - name: Install Rust
        run: |
          rustup component add rustfmt
          rustup component add clippy

      - name: Install cargo-deny
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-deny@0.19.0

      - name: Format
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

      - name: Clippy (all features)
        run: cargo clippy --all --all-targets --all-features -- -Dwarnings

      - name: Clippy (no features)
        run: cargo clippy --all --all-targets --no-default-features -- -Dwarnings

      - name: License check
        run: cargo deny --workspace --all-features check licenses

      - name: Advisory check
        run: cargo deny --workspace check advisories

      - name: Ban check
        run: cargo deny --workspace check bans

      - name: Source check
        run: cargo deny --workspace check sources

  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Compile checks across feature combinations
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  compile:
    name: Compile (${{ matrix.name }})
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      RUSTFLAGS: --deny warnings
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: default
            args: "--all --all-targets"
          - name: all-features
            args: "--all --all-targets --all-features"
          - name: no-features
            args: "--all --all-targets --no-default-features"
          # Release-mode variants catch bugs that debug-only assertions or
          # cfg(debug_assertions)-gated fields hide. Without these, code that
          # references a debug-only field outside a cfg gate compiles cleanly
          # in debug CI but breaks at the user's release build.
          - name: release-default
            args: "--release --all --all-targets"
          - name: release-all-features
            args: "--release --all --all-targets --all-features"
          - name: release-no-features
            args: "--release --all --all-targets --no-default-features"
          - name: wasm32
            args: ""
            wasm: true
          # Cortex-M0+ has no native pointer-width atomic CAS, so it is the
          # target that actually exercises the portable-atomic-util Arc and the
          # critical-section CAS strategy that Cargo.toml enables for every
          # build. wasm32 does not: it has the atomics available and selects
          # different code. Without this entry the RP2040 support the manifest
          # claims, and pays a per-atomic critical section for, is never
          # compiled. See issue #374.
          - name: thumbv6m
            args: ""
            embedded: thumbv6m-none-eabi
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/bin/
            ~/.cargo/registry/index/
            ~/.cargo/registry/cache/
            ~/.cargo/git/db/
            target/
          key: compile-${{ matrix.name }}-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.toml', '**/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: compile-${{ matrix.name }}-

      - name: Compile
        if: ${{ !matrix.wasm && !matrix.embedded }}
        run: cargo check ${{ matrix.args }}

      - name: Compile (${{ matrix.embedded }})
        if: ${{ matrix.embedded }}
        run: |
          rustup target add ${{ matrix.embedded }}
          # Bare-metal target: lib only. There is no std, so no test harness,
          # no build scripts that assume a host, and no dev-dependencies.
          cargo check -p shodh-redb --target ${{ matrix.embedded }} --no-default-features --lib

      - name: Compile (wasm32-unknown-unknown)
        if: ${{ matrix.wasm }}
        run: |
          rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown
          # Ensure lockfile exists (cargo pkgid requires it)
          test -f Cargo.lock || cargo generate-lockfile
          command="cargo check -p $(cargo pkgid) -p shodh-redb-derive --target wasm32-unknown-unknown"
          $command
          $command --features std,logging,cache_metrics,compression_lz4,compression_zstd
          $command --no-default-features

  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Test matrix: multi-platform
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  test:
    name: Test (${{ matrix.name }})
    needs: [lint, compile]
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: Linux x86_64
            os: ubuntu-latest
            fuzz: true
            wasi: true
            python: true
            recall: true
          - name: Linux ARM64
            os: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            fuzz: true
            wasi: true
            python: true
          - name: macOS
            os: macos-latest
            fuzz: true
            wasi: true
            python: true
          - name: Windows
            os: windows-latest
            fuzz: false
            wasi: false
            python: true

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}
    env:
      RUSTFLAGS: --deny warnings

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/bin/
            ~/.cargo/registry/index/
            ~/.cargo/registry/cache/
            ~/.cargo/git/db/
            target/
            fuzz/target/
          key: test-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.toml', '**/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: test-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-

      - name: Non ASCII characters
        if: startsWith(matrix.os, 'ubuntu')
        run: |
            if grep -P -n "[^\x00-\x7F]" -r --include="*.rs" --include="*.toml" .; then
            echo "Non-ASCII characters detected"
            exit 1
            fi

      - name: Install Python
        uses: actions/setup-python@v5
        with:
          python-version: "3.12"

      - name: Install Rust
        run: |
          rustup component add rustfmt
          rustup component add clippy

      - name: OSX x86 rust
        if: startsWith(matrix.os, 'macos')
        run: rustup target add x86_64-apple-darwin

      - name: Setup wasmtime
        if: matrix.wasi
        uses: bytecodealliance/actions/wasmtime/setup@v1
        with:
          version: "24.0.0"

      - name: Clean stale cargo-fuzz
        if: matrix.fuzz
        run: rm -f ~/.cargo/bin/cargo-fuzz
        shell: bash

      - name: Install cargo-fuzz
        if: matrix.fuzz
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-fuzz@0.13.1

      - name: Setup fuzz toolchain
        if: matrix.fuzz
        run: |
          rustup install nightly
          HOST_TARGET=$(rustc -vV | awk '/^host:/ {print $2}')
          rustup target add --toolchain nightly "$HOST_TARGET"

      - name: Install just
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: just@1.36.0

      - name: Build all
        run: cargo build --all --all-targets --all-features

      - name: Run tests
        run: cargo test --all --all-features
        env:
          RUST_BACKTRACE: "1"

      - name: Clear stale fuzz corpus
        if: matrix.fuzz
        run: rm -rf fuzz/corpus/ fuzz/artifacts/

      - name: Fuzzer (60s core + 30s each new target)
        if: matrix.fuzz
        run: |
          HOST_TARGET=$(rustc -vV | awk '/^host:/ {print $2}')
          # fuzz_redb does DB create + crash recovery + compaction + integrity check per input.
          # Timeouts are expected on GHA shared runners (slow I/O) and are not real bugs.
          # Only fail on crash/assertion artifacts, not timeout artifacts.
          cargo +nightly fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" fuzz_redb -- -max_len=10000 -max_total_time=60 -timeout=300 || {
            exit_code=$?
            # Check if all artifacts are timeouts (not crashes)
            if ls fuzz/artifacts/fuzz_redb/timeout-* 1>/dev/null 2>&1 && ! ls fuzz/artifacts/fuzz_redb/crash-* 1>/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "::warning::fuzz_redb produced timeout artifacts only (expected on slow runners)"
            else
              exit $exit_code
            fi
          }
          for target in fuzz_db_image fuzz_cdc_deser fuzz_cluster_blob fuzz_incremental_deser fuzz_merge_ops fuzz_pq_codebook; do
            cargo +nightly fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" "$target" -- -max_len=10000 -max_total_time=30 -timeout=30
          done
        env:
          # Cleared so a RUSTFLAGS inherited from the environment cannot change
          # what cargo-fuzz builds. cargo-fuzz appends its own flags to this.
          RUSTFLAGS: ""
          # Debug assertions are ON here, deliberately. See fuzz/Cargo.toml for
          # why. A CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG_ASSERTIONS: "false" used to sit
          # in this block claiming to turn them off; it never did anything --
          # cargo-fuzz reads no such variable, it appends -Cdebug-assertions to
          # RUSTFLAGS, and that beats any profile setting.

      # Keep the reproducer. cargo-fuzz writes the failing input to
      # fuzz/artifacts/, and without this it is discarded when the runner is
      # torn down -- the only recovery being to scrape the base64 blob out of
      # the log. The nightly job already uploads; PR CI did not, which is where
      # most crashes are actually found.
      - name: Upload fuzz artifacts
        if: failure() && matrix.fuzz
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: fuzz-artifacts-${{ matrix.os }}-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: fuzz/artifacts/
          if-no-files-found: ignore
          retention-days: 30

      # IVF-PQ recall gate. Release mode, one platform only.
      #
      # The tests are `#[ignore]`d and invoked explicitly here because a debug
      # build of this scalar float path is roughly 21x slower (151s vs 7s to
      # build one index at the gate geometry). Left un-ignored they would run
      # inside every debug test job and add about ten minutes to each, for no
      # signal a single release run does not already give.
      #
      # `--skip deep_` leaves out the realistic-geometry tier, which is a
      # by-hand measuring stick for quantization changes rather than a gate.
      - name: IVF-PQ recall gate
        if: matrix.recall
        run: cargo test --release --test ivfpq_recall_tests -- --ignored --nocapture --skip deep_

      # ── CLI smoke tests ──
      - name: CLI smoke test (Unix)
        if: runner.os != 'Windows'
        run: |
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli --example create_test_db
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- info test.redb
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- tables test.redb
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- stats test.redb
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- header test.redb
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- dump test.redb -t users -l 5
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- verify test.redb
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- compact test.redb
          rm test.redb

      - name: CLI smoke test (Windows)
        if: runner.os == 'Windows'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli --example create_test_db
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- info test.redb
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- tables test.redb
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- stats test.redb
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- header test.redb
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- dump test.redb -t users -l 5
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- verify test.redb
          cargo run -p shodh-redb-cli -- compact test.redb
          rm test.redb

      # ── Python binding tests ──
      - name: Python tests (Unix)
        if: matrix.python && runner.os != 'Windows'
        run: |
          python3 -m venv venv
          source venv/bin/activate
          pip3 install --upgrade pip
          pip3 install maturin
          maturin develop --manifest-path=./crates/redb-python/Cargo.toml
          python3 -m unittest discover --start-directory=./crates/redb-python

      - name: Python tests (Windows)
        if: matrix.python && runner.os == 'Windows'
        run: |
          python3 -m venv venv
          venv\Scripts\activate
          pip3 install --upgrade pip
          pip3 install maturin
          maturin develop --manifest-path=./crates/redb-python/Cargo.toml
          python3 -m unittest discover --start-directory=./crates/redb-python

      # ── WASI tests ──
      - name: WASI tests
        if: matrix.wasi
        run: RUSTFLAGS="" just test_wasi

  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Feature-isolated test runs (ubuntu-latest only)
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  test-features:
    name: Test Features (${{ matrix.name }})
    needs: [lint, compile]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    env:
      RUSTFLAGS: --deny warnings
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - name: no-default-features
            args: "--no-default-features"
          - name: default
            args: ""
          - name: compression_lz4
            args: "--features compression_lz4"
          - name: compression_zstd
            args: "--features compression_zstd"
          # Release-mode test variants catch bugs that only surface under
          # optimized builds (e.g. cfg(debug_assertions)-gated fields, UB
          # masked by debug zero-init, op-rate-sensitive resource bounds).
          - name: release-default
            args: "--release"
          - name: release-all-features
            args: "--release --all-features"
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/bin/
            ~/.cargo/registry/index/
            ~/.cargo/registry/cache/
            ~/.cargo/git/db/
            target/
          key: test-features-${{ matrix.name }}-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.toml', '**/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: test-features-${{ matrix.name }}-

      - name: Run tests (${{ matrix.name }})
        run: cargo test --all ${{ matrix.args }}
        env:
          RUST_BACKTRACE: "1"

  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  # MSRV check: ensure we compile and pass tests on minimum supported Rust
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  msrv:
    name: MSRV (1.89)
    needs: lint
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install MSRV toolchain
        run: |
          rustup toolchain install 1.89.0 --profile minimal
          rustup override set 1.89.0

      - name: Cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/registry/index/
            ~/.cargo/registry/cache/
            ~/.cargo/git/db/
            target/
          key: msrv-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.toml', '**/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: msrv-

      - name: Check MSRV
        run: cargo check --all --all-features

      - name: Test MSRV
        run: cargo test --all --all-features
        env:
          RUST_BACKTRACE: "1"

  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Summary gate for branch protection
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  ci-pass:
    name: CI Pass
    if: always()
    needs: [lint, compile, test, test-features, msrv]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check all jobs
        run: |
          if [[ "${{ needs.lint.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "Lint failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.compile.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "Compile failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.test.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "Test failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.test-features.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "Test Features failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          if [[ "${{ needs.msrv.result }}" != "success" ]]; then
            echo "MSRV failed"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "All checks passed"

name: Benchmarks

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - master
  pull_request:

concurrency:
  group: bench-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # GATE: Pure-compute benchmarks (vector_ops)
  #
  # On PRs: check out master, build a fresh baseline, then switch to
  # the PR branch and compare -- all in the same job on the same runner.
  # This eliminates cross-run variance from different runner hardware.
  #
  # On master pushes: no comparison needed (baseline is always fresh).
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  bench-gate:
    name: Performance Gate (vector ops)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # Fetch enough history to check out both master and the PR branch.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/bin/
            ~/.cargo/registry/index/
            ~/.cargo/registry/cache/
            ~/.cargo/git/db/
            target/
          key: bench-gate-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.toml', '**/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: bench-gate-${{ runner.os }}-

      - name: Install Rust
        run: rustup component add rustfmt

      - name: Stabilize CPU for benchmarking
        run: |
          # Pin CPU governor to performance mode (constant frequency, no scaling)
          if command -v cpupower &>/dev/null; then
            sudo cpupower frequency-set -g performance || true
          fi
          # Disable turbo boost to prevent thermal throttling variance
          if [ -f /sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_pstate/no_turbo ]; then
            echo 1 | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_pstate/no_turbo || true
          fi
          if [ -f /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/boost ]; then
            echo 0 | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/boost || true
          fi

      - name: Run vector_ops benchmarks
        run: |
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            # Step 1: Build baseline from master on THIS runner.
            git checkout ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
            cargo bench --bench criterion_vector_ops -p shodh-redb \
              -- --save-baseline master 2>&1

            # Cooldown: let CPU thermal state settle between runs
            sleep 10

            # Step 2: Switch back to PR branch and compare.
            git checkout ${{ github.sha }}
            cargo bench --bench criterion_vector_ops -p shodh-redb \
              -- --baseline master 2>&1 | tee bench_gate_output.txt

            # Detect real regressions vs. CI noise.
            #
            # Shared GitHub runners introduce 10-35% variance from thermal
            # throttling, CPU frequency scaling, and noisy neighbours. The
            # baseline always runs first (cool CPU) and the PR second (warm
            # CPU), creating a systematic bias toward false regressions.
            #
            # Strategy: pair each criterion "regressed" verdict with the
            # preceding time-change line. Only count regressions where the
            # point estimate (middle value) is >= 20%. Then fail only if a
            # majority of benchmarks show such regressions AND at least 3
            # are affected (ruling out one-off outliers).
            # Count regressions where the estimate (second percentage in the
            # time: change line) is >= 20%. Criterion format:
            #   time:   [+31.2% +33.1% +34.5%] (p = ...)
            #   thrpt:  [...]
            #   Performance has regressed.
            SIGNIFICANT=$(awk '
              /time:.*\[/ { last_time = $0 }
              /Performance has regressed/ {
                n = split(last_time, a, " ")
                for (i = 1; i <= n; i++) {
                  if (a[i] ~ /^\+[0-9]/) {
                    gsub(/[+%]/, "", a[i])
                    if (a[i]+0 >= 20.0) significant++
                    break
                  }
                }
              }
              END { print significant+0 }
            ' bench_gate_output.txt)
            REGRESSED=$(grep -c "regressed" bench_gate_output.txt || true)
            IMPROVED=$(grep -c "improved" bench_gate_output.txt || true)
            TOTAL=$((REGRESSED + IMPROVED))
            echo "Benchmark results: $REGRESSED regressed ($SIGNIFICANT >= 20%), $IMPROVED improved out of $TOTAL changed"
            if [ "$TOTAL" -gt 0 ] && [ "$SIGNIFICANT" -gt $((TOTAL / 2)) ] && [ "$SIGNIFICANT" -ge 3 ]; then
              echo ""
              echo "============================================================"
              echo "REGRESSION DETECTED: $SIGNIFICANT/$TOTAL benchmarks regressed >= 20%."
              echo "Baseline and PR measured on the same runner."
              echo "============================================================"
              echo ""
              grep -B2 "regressed" bench_gate_output.txt
              exit 1
            fi
          else
            # Master push: just run benchmarks (no comparison needed).
            cargo bench --bench criterion_vector_ops -p shodh-redb \
              -- --save-baseline master
          fi
        env:
          RUSTFLAGS: ""

  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  # ADVISORY: I/O-bound benchmarks (kv, blob, ivfpq)
  #
  # These involve disk writes, file creation, and memory allocation.
  # Shared GitHub Actions runners introduce 30-50% wall-time variance
  # on I/O workloads, making hard gates unreliable. Instead, we post
  # an advisory comment on PRs with benchmark-action (15% comment
  # threshold) and NEVER fail CI.
  # ------------------------------------------------------------------
  bench-report:
    name: Benchmark Report (I/O)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pull-requests: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          # The same-runner baseline checks out the PR base commit, so the
          # default shallow clone is not enough.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - name: Cache cargo
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/bin/
            ~/.cargo/registry/index/
            ~/.cargo/registry/cache/
            ~/.cargo/git/db/
            target/
          key: bench-report-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.toml', '**/Cargo.lock') }}
          restore-keys: bench-report-${{ runner.os }}-
      - name: Install Rust
        run: rustup component add rustfmt

      # Same CPU stabilisation as the vector_ops gate. Without it, frequency
      # scaling and turbo/thermal behaviour add variance that swamps the signal.
      - name: Stabilize CPU for benchmarking
        run: |
          if command -v cpupower &>/dev/null; then
            sudo cpupower frequency-set -g performance || true
          fi
          if [ -f /sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_pstate/no_turbo ]; then
            echo 1 | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/intel_pstate/no_turbo || true
          fi
          if [ -f /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/boost ]; then
            echo 0 | sudo tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpufreq/boost || true
          fi

      # Build the baseline on THIS runner, mirroring the vector_ops gate.
      #
      # The previous implementation restored a `.bench_baseline.json` written by
      # an earlier run on a DIFFERENT GitHub runner, so every comparison
      # measured the difference between two machines rather than between two
      # commits. That produced +/-30-62% apparent variance (e.g. kv/insert/1000
      # reported 2377594 ns +/- 1468337) and systematic-looking "improvements"
      # where six benchmarks all landed at ratio 0.88-0.94 simultaneously --
      # the signature of a faster runner, not faster code. At that noise level
      # the suite could not detect a real 20% regression, which is why it could
      # never be promoted from advisory to gating.
      - name: Run I/O benchmarks
        id: run_bench
        run: |
          BENCHES="--bench criterion_kv --bench criterion_blob --bench criterion_ivfpq"
          if [ "${{ github.event_name }}" = "pull_request" ]; then
            git checkout ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
            cargo bench $BENCHES -p shodh-redb -- --save-baseline base 2>&1 | tail -20

            # Let page cache, disk queue and thermal state settle so the second
            # run is not measuring the first run's after-effects.
            sync || true
            sleep 15

            git checkout ${{ github.sha }}
            cargo bench $BENCHES -p shodh-redb -- --baseline base 2>&1 | tee bench_io_output.txt
          else
            cargo bench $BENCHES -p shodh-redb -- --save-baseline base 2>&1 | tee bench_io_output.txt
          fi
        env:
          RUSTFLAGS: ""

      # Advisory: surface criterion's own same-runner verdict. Not a gate yet --
      # promoting this to a required check should be a separate, deliberate
      # change once we have seen the real noise floor across several PRs.
      # Advisory: post criterion's same-runner verdict as a single sticky PR
      # comment, updated in place rather than appended each run.
      #
      # The comment is deliberately kept (the previous implementation had one
      # via github-action-benchmark): an advisory signal that lives only in the
      # Actions UI does not reach reviewers, so it does not influence decisions.
      # What changed is the data behind it -- same-runner comparison instead of
      # cross-runner JSON.
      #
      # Not a gate yet: promoting this to a required check should be a separate,
      # deliberate change once the real noise floor has been observed across
      # several PRs.
      - name: Report I/O comparison
        if: always() && github.event_name == 'pull_request'
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          PR: ${{ github.event.pull_request.number }}
          BASE_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }}
        run: |
          MARKER="<!-- shodh-redb-io-bench -->"
          {
            echo "$MARKER"
            echo "### I/O benchmarks (advisory)"
            echo ""
          } > comment.md

          if [ ! -s bench_io_output.txt ]; then
            echo "No benchmark output was produced -- the suite failed to run." >> comment.md
          else
            REGRESSED=$(grep -c "Performance has regressed" bench_io_output.txt || true)
            IMPROVED=$(grep -c "Performance has improved" bench_io_output.txt || true)
            NOISE=$(grep -c "within noise threshold" bench_io_output.txt || true)
            NOCHANGE=$(grep -c "No change in performance" bench_io_output.txt || true)
            {
              echo "| verdict | count |"
              echo "|---|---|"
              echo "| regressed | **$REGRESSED** |"
              echo "| improved | $IMPROVED |"
              echo "| within noise | $NOISE |"
              echo "| no change | $NOCHANGE |"
              echo ""
              echo "Baseline is \`${BASE_SHA:0:7}\` benchmarked on **this same runner**, so"
              echo "cross-machine variance is excluded. Advisory only -- does not gate."
              echo ""
              if [ "$REGRESSED" -gt 0 ]; then
                echo "<details><summary>Regressions</summary>"
                echo ""
                echo '```'
                grep -B 4 "Performance has regressed" bench_io_output.txt | head -80
                echo '```'
                echo ""
                echo "</details>"
                echo ""
              fi
              echo "<details><summary>Full comparison</summary>"
              echo ""
              echo '```'
              grep -E "time:|change:|Performance has|within noise|No change" bench_io_output.txt | head -150
              echo '```'
              echo ""
              echo "</details>"
            } >> comment.md
          fi

          # Update the existing sticky comment if present, else create it.
          ID=$(gh api "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${PR}/comments" --paginate                  --jq "[.[] | select(.body | startswith(\"$MARKER\"))] | .[0].id // empty")
          if [ -n "$ID" ]; then
            gh api -X PATCH "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/comments/${ID}"               -F body=@comment.md >/dev/null
            echo "updated comment $ID"
          else
            gh api -X POST "repos/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY}/issues/${PR}/comments"               -F body=@comment.md >/dev/null
            echo "created comment"
          fi

          cat comment.md >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

name: Fuzz Regressions

# Replays every input in fuzz/regressions/ under AddressSanitizer.
#
# Manual trigger, because its two jobs are different: as regression coverage it
# is cheap and deterministic, and as a diagnosis tool it is how a stack trace
# gets captured for a hang that cannot be reproduced locally -- cargo-fuzz does
# not link on Windows MSVC, so a Linux runner is the only option available.
on:
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  replay:
    name: Replay known fuzz inputs
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install nightly
        run: rustup toolchain install nightly --profile minimal

      - name: Install cargo-fuzz
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-fuzz@0.13.1

      # cargo-fuzz defaults --target to the triple it was built for, and the
      # installed binary is musl-linked. See the same fix in nightly.yml.
      - name: Resolve host target
        run: echo "HOST_TARGET=$(rustc -vV | awk '/^host:/ {print $2}')" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      # Without a symbolizer AddressSanitizer prints raw addresses, which is
      # useless for diagnosis -- the whole point of running under ASan here.
      # rustup ships one with llvm-tools; fall back to the distro package.
      - name: Locate llvm-symbolizer
        run: |
          rustup component add llvm-tools --toolchain nightly || true
          sym=$(find "$(rustc +nightly --print sysroot)" -name 'llvm-symbolizer' -type f 2>/dev/null | head -1)
          if [ -z "$sym" ]; then
            sym=$(command -v llvm-symbolizer || true)
          fi
          if [ -z "$sym" ]; then
            sym=$(ls /usr/lib/llvm-*/bin/llvm-symbolizer 2>/dev/null | head -1)
          fi
          if [ -z "$sym" ]; then
            echo "::error::no llvm-symbolizer found; stacks would be unsymbolized"
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "using $sym"
          echo "ASAN_SYMBOLIZER_PATH=$sym" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          echo "ASAN_OPTIONS=symbolize=1:print_stacktrace=1" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Replay
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          status=0
          for dir in fuzz/regressions/*/; do
            target=$(basename "$dir")
            for input in "$dir"*; do
              name=$(basename "$input")
              echo "::group::$target $name"
              # AddressSanitizer so a hang or crash prints a stack. -timeout=30
              # bounds a hang: libFuzzer reports rather than running to the
              # 1200s default.
              if cargo +nightly fuzz run --sanitizer=address \
                   --target "$HOST_TARGET" "$target" "$input" -- -timeout=30; then
                echo "$target $name: ok"
              else
                echo "::error::$target failed on $name"
                status=1
              fi
              echo "::endgroup::"
            done
          done
          exit $status

name: Release

on:
  push:
    tags:
      # Releases are tagged `shodh-v*` to preserve upstream redb's existing
      # `v0.5.0` .. `v4.x.x` tag history. The trigger previously matched only
      # `v*`, so `shodh-v0.5.0` never fired it and 0.5.0 shipped with no
      # GitHub release artifacts at all -- the last successful run was v0.3.3.
      # Both patterns are kept so old-style tags still work.
      - "v*"
      - "shodh-v*"

permissions:
  contents: write

jobs:
  build:
    name: Build (${{ matrix.target }})
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - target: x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu
            os: ubuntu-latest
            archive: tar.gz
          - target: aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu
            os: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            archive: tar.gz
          - target: x86_64-apple-darwin
            os: macos-latest
            archive: tar.gz
          - target: aarch64-apple-darwin
            os: macos-latest
            archive: tar.gz
          - target: x86_64-pc-windows-msvc
            os: windows-latest
            archive: zip

    runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Install Rust
        run: |
          rustup target add ${{ matrix.target }}

      - name: Install cross-compilation tools (aarch64-apple-darwin)
        if: matrix.target == 'aarch64-apple-darwin'
        run: |
          # macOS runners are already ARM64; this target compiles natively
          echo "Native ARM64 build on macOS runner"

      - name: Build release binaries
        run: |
          cargo build --release --target ${{ matrix.target }} -p shodh-redb-cli

      - name: Package (Unix)
        if: matrix.archive == 'tar.gz'
        run: |
          STAGING="shodh-redb-${{ github.ref_name }}-${{ matrix.target }}"
          mkdir -p "$STAGING"
          cp "target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/shodh-redb" "$STAGING/"
          cp LICENSE* README.md "$STAGING/" 2>/dev/null || true
          tar czf "$STAGING.tar.gz" "$STAGING"
          echo "ASSET=$STAGING.tar.gz" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Package (Windows)
        if: matrix.archive == 'zip'
        shell: bash
        run: |
          STAGING="shodh-redb-${{ github.ref_name }}-${{ matrix.target }}"
          mkdir -p "$STAGING"
          cp "target/${{ matrix.target }}/release/shodh-redb.exe" "$STAGING/"
          cp LICENSE* README.md "$STAGING/" 2>/dev/null || true
          7z a "$STAGING.zip" "$STAGING"
          echo "ASSET=$STAGING.zip" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Upload artifact
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: release-${{ matrix.target }}
          path: ${{ env.ASSET }}
          retention-days: 1

  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  # Create GitHub Release with all artifacts
  # ──────────────────────────────────────────────
  release:
    name: GitHub Release
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Download all artifacts
        uses: actions/download-artifact@v4
        with:
          path: artifacts/
          pattern: release-*
          merge-multiple: true

      - name: Generate checksums
        run: |
          cd artifacts
          sha256sum * > checksums-sha256.txt
          cat checksums-sha256.txt

      - name: Create release
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          generate_release_notes: true
          files: |
            artifacts/*
        env:
          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

name: Nightly

on:
  schedule:
    - cron: "0 3 * * *" # Every day at 03:00 UTC
  # Manual trigger. Without this the only way to find out whether a change to
  # this workflow works is to wait for 03:00 UTC, which is how it stayed broken
  # for three months.
  workflow_dispatch:

jobs:
  # Debug assertions are ON in every fuzz build here, deliberately -- see
  # fuzz/Cargo.toml. This job used to set CARGO_PROFILE_RELEASE_DEBUG_ASSERTIONS
  # to "false" to turn them off; cargo-fuzz reads no such variable, so it never
  # did anything, and the assertions are worth keeping regardless.
  extended-fuzz:
    name: Extended Fuzzing
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Cache
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: |
            ~/.cargo/bin/
            ~/.cargo/registry/index/
            ~/.cargo/registry/cache/
            ~/.cargo/git/db/
            target/
            fuzz/target/
          key: fuzz-build-${{ hashFiles('**/Cargo.toml', 'fuzz/**') }}
          restore-keys: fuzz-build-

      # The corpus is cached separately from the build, and deliberately not
      # under a content-derived key.
      #
      # It used to share the build cache above, whose key hashes `fuzz/**`. The
      # corpus is gitignored, so at restore time that hash only covers the fuzz
      # SOURCE, which rarely changes -- so the key hit EXACTLY, and
      # `actions/cache` skips saving on an exact hit. The corpus was therefore
      # frozen at whatever it held the first run after a fuzz-source change and
      # never grew again.
      #
      # That is fatal for coverage-guided fuzzing, which is a search that only
      # pays off as the corpus accumulates. Every night was re-running a cold
      # search over shallow states, which is why defects here surface strictly
      # one at a time, each only once the previous one stops blocking the path.
      #
      # `run_id` is unique per run, so the key never hits exactly and the save
      # always happens; `restore-keys` then picks up the most recent corpus.
      - name: Restore fuzz corpus
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v4
        with:
          path: fuzz/corpus
          key: fuzz-corpus-${{ github.run_id }}
          restore-keys: fuzz-corpus-

      - name: Install Rust
        run: |
          rustup component add rustfmt
          rustup component add clippy

      - name: Install tools
        uses: taiki-e/install-action@v2
        with:
          tool: cargo-fuzz@0.13.1,cargo-deny@0.19.0

      # cargo-fuzz defaults --target to the triple it was itself built for, and
      # taiki-e/install-action ships a musl-linked binary. Without an explicit
      # --target every step below tried to build for x86_64-unknown-linux-musl,
      # whose std the runner does not have, and the job died at
      # "could not compile cfg-if" before a single input was fuzzed. That is why
      # this workflow failed 100 nightlies in a row. ci.yml already resolves the
      # host triple this way; nightly never got the same fix.
      - name: Resolve host target
        run: echo "HOST_TARGET=$(rustc -vV | awk '/^host:/ {print $2}')" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"

      - name: Fuzz redb core (5 minutes)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" fuzz_redb -- -max_len=10000 -max_total_time=900

      - name: Fuzz crafted database images (5 minutes)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" fuzz_db_image -- -max_len=4096 -max_total_time=600

      - name: Fuzz vector ops (90s)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" fuzz_vector_ops -- -max_len=10000 -max_total_time=240

      - name: Fuzz quantization (90s)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" fuzz_quantization -- -max_len=10000 -max_total_time=240

      - name: Fuzz blob types (60s)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" fuzz_blob_types -- -max_len=10000 -max_total_time=240

      - name: Fuzz IVF-PQ kmeans (90s)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" fuzz_ivfpq_kmeans -- -max_len=10000 -max_total_time=240

      # Every [[bin]] in fuzz/Cargo.toml must appear in this job or in ci.yml.
      # fuzz_ivfpq_index was in neither, so it had never been run at all.
      - name: Fuzz IVF-PQ index (90s)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" fuzz_ivfpq_index -- -max_len=10000 -max_total_time=240

      - name: Fuzz CDC deser (90s)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" fuzz_cdc_deser -- -max_len=10000 -max_total_time=240

      - name: Fuzz cluster blob (90s)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" fuzz_cluster_blob -- -max_len=10000 -max_total_time=240

      - name: Fuzz incremental deser (90s)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" fuzz_incremental_deser -- -max_len=10000 -max_total_time=240

      - name: Fuzz merge ops (90s)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" fuzz_merge_ops -- -max_len=10000 -max_total_time=240

      - name: Fuzz PQ codebook (90s)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo fuzz run --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" fuzz_pq_codebook -- -max_len=10000 -max_total_time=240

      # Every fuzz step above runs with `continue-on-error`, so one target
      # cannot skip the other eleven -- which is exactly what happened the first
      # time this job built successfully: `fuzz_redb` hung and the remaining
      # eleven targets never executed, giving zero coverage from them.
      #
      # The job's verdict comes from the artifacts instead. cargo-fuzz writes a
      # crash-* or timeout-* file only when a target actually fails, so their
      # presence is the signal. Deliberately NOT tolerant of timeouts: a hang is
      # a defect, and treating it as noise is how the fuzz_redb hang survived in
      # PR CI for months behind an "expected on slow runners" warning.
      - name: Check fuzz artifacts
        run: |
          shopt -s nullglob
          found=(fuzz/artifacts/*/crash-* fuzz/artifacts/*/timeout-* fuzz/artifacts/*/oom-*)
          if [ ${#found[@]} -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::fuzzing produced ${#found[@]} failure artifact(s)"
            for f in "${found[@]}"; do
              echo "  $f"
            done
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "no crash, timeout, or OOM artifacts"

      # An accumulating corpus is the point, but an unminimised one becomes its
      # own problem: libFuzzer replays every input at startup, so unchecked
      # growth converts the budget above from exploration into replay, and the
      # cache has a size limit that evicts LRU. `cmin` keeps the smallest set of
      # inputs that preserves coverage.
      #
      # Best-effort: a cmin failure must not fail the run or skip the save, and
      # a target whose corpus is still empty has nothing to minimise.
      - name: Minimise fuzz corpus
        if: always()
        continue-on-error: true
        run: |
          for dir in fuzz/corpus/*/; do
            [ -d "$dir" ] || continue
            target=$(basename "$dir")
            [ -n "$(ls -A "$dir" 2>/dev/null)" ] || continue
            echo "cmin $target ($(ls -1 "$dir" | wc -l) inputs)"
            cargo fuzz cmin --sanitizer=none --target "$HOST_TARGET" "$target" ||               echo "::warning::cmin failed for $target, keeping the unminimised corpus"
          done

      # Must run even when a target failed: a run that found a crash has by
      # definition explored new territory, and that is exactly the corpus worth
      # keeping.
      - name: Save fuzz corpus
        if: always()
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: fuzz/corpus
          key: fuzz-corpus-${{ github.run_id }}

      - name: Upload corpus and artifacts
        if: always()
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        with:
          name: fuzz-artifacts-${{ github.run_id }}
          path: |
            fuzz/artifacts/
            fuzz/corpus/
          retention-days: 30

[workspace.package]

license = "Apache-2.0"
homepage = "https://github.com/varun29ankuS/shodh-redb"
repository = "https://github.com/varun29ankuS/shodh-redb"
authors = ["Varun Sharma"]

[dependencies]
log = { version = "0.4.17", optional = true }
chrono_v0_4 = { package = "chrono", version= "0.4.41", optional = true }
uuid = { version= "1.17.0", optional = true }
lz4_flex = { version = "0.11.5", optional = true }
sha2 = { version = "0.10", default-features = false }
zstd = { version = "0.13.3", optional = true, default-features = false }
hashbrown = "0.15"
portable-atomic = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["fallback"] }
spin = { version = "0.10", default-features = false, features = ["mutex", "spin_mutex", "rwlock", "portable-atomic"] }

# Targets without native pointer-width atomic CAS (e.g. thumbv6m / Cortex-M0+,
# including the RP2040) cannot use `alloc::sync::Arc`. portable-atomic-util
# provides a CAS-free Arc, and portable-atomic needs a CAS strategy.
#
# `critical-section` is enabled HERE rather than as a crate feature on purpose:
# it makes portable-atomic take a critical section for *every* atomic
# operation, which would be a severe regression on targets that have native
# atomics. Scoping it to this target table means `--all-features` cannot
# accidentally turn it on for x86_64/aarch64.
#
# The final binary must supply a critical-section implementation (e.g. the
# `cortex-m` crate's `critical-section-single-core` feature, or `embassy-rp`
# on RP2040). Single-core targets that can guarantee it may instead build with
# RUSTFLAGS="--cfg portable_atomic_unsafe_assume_single_core", which is faster
# because loads and stores then avoid disabling interrupts.
[target.'cfg(not(target_has_atomic = "ptr"))'.dependencies]
portable-atomic-util = { version = "0.2", default-features = false, features = ["alloc"] }
portable-atomic = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["fallback", "critical-section"] }

[target.'cfg(target_os = "wasi")'.dependencies]
libc = "0.2.174"

[target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'.dependencies]

[target.'cfg(unix)'.dependencies]

[target.'cfg(target_os = "windows")'.dependencies]

    "Win32_System_Threading",

] }

# for backwards compatibility testing - pin at 2.6.0

[![Crates.io](https://img.shields.io/crates/v/shodh-redb.svg)](https://crates.io/crates/shodh-redb)
[![Documentation](https://docs.rs/shodh-redb/badge.svg)](https://docs.rs/shodh-redb)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue)](LICENSE)
[![CI](https://github.com/varun29ankuS/shodh-redb/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/varun29ankuS/shodh-redb/actions)
[![no_std](https://img.shields.io/badge/no__std-compatible-green)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/reference/names/preludes.html#the-no_std-attribute)

**Embedded multi-modal database engine for edge AI.** Key-value, vector search (IVF-PQ), blob storage, TTL, merge operators, CDC, composite queries -- all in one ACID-transactional file with a `no_std` core.

95% recall@1 at 1,000+ QPS on SIFT1M. 1.6--3x faster writes than LMDB, 2--3x faster reads than RocksDB. Single-threaded. 8 GB RAM. No GPU.

| Vector search | IVF-PQ | flat scan | -- | -- | HNSW |
| Blob storage | built-in | external | -- | -- | -- |
| TTL / expiration | per-key | manual | -- | TTL CF | -- |
| CDC | built-in | triggers | -- | -- | -- |
| Merge operators | built-in | -- | -- | built-in | -- |
| `no_std` / wasm | core lib | -- | -- | -- | -- |

| File format | single file | single file | single file | LSM dir | server |

## When to choose shodh-redb

shodh-redb occupies a specific niche: **embedded Rust applications that need KV + vector search + blob storage in a single ACID-transactional process**. It is not a drop-in replacement for any single tool above; it replaces *combinations* of them.

**Choose shodh-redb when:**
- You need vector similarity search and KV in the same process, and you do not want to compose `RocksDB + FAISS` (or `LMDB + hnswlib`) yourself.
- You ship a single Rust binary and want to avoid a C++ dependency or a separate vector-database service.
- You target embedded / `no_std` / `wasm32` and need a real B-tree, not a sled-style log.
- Your workload is read-heavy or read/write balanced at single-host scale (gigabytes to low terabytes).
- You want a small, auditable codebase (~50K LOC core) instead of a 600K-LOC C++ project.

**Choose something else when:**
- **You need RocksDB's write-optimized LSM**: shodh-redb is a B-tree. For sustained 100K+ writes/sec at multi-terabyte scale, RocksDB's LSM architecture wins by design.
- **You need multiple writer processes** or shared-database concurrency. shodh-redb is single-process, single-writer (`try_lock` enforced). Use a server database (Postgres, Qdrant, MongoDB) instead.
- **You need state-of-the-art ANN recall**. IVF-PQ is a solid baseline; for graph indexes (HNSW, DiskANN) at the recall/latency frontier, use Qdrant, Milvus, or FAISS directly.
- **You need a query language** (SQL, Cypher). shodh-redb is a programmatic API.
- **You require Jepsen-grade crash-safety evidence**. The B-tree engine inherits redb's COW + checksum design, but no formal linearizability tests have been published.

The published benchmark numbers (1.6–3× writes vs LMDB, 2–3× reads vs RocksDB) are at single-host, single-thread, 5M-key scale on the workloads in `crates/redb-bench`. They are real, reproducible micro-benchmarks -- not extrapolations to RocksDB's strong regime (large-scale, write-heavy, concurrent).

---

## Why shodh-redb?

Every edge vector database (sqlite-vec, LanceDB, Qdrant) bolts vector search onto a storage engine that wasn't designed for it. shodh-redb builds both from the same B-tree:

- **Vector search** -- IVF-PQ with integer ADC, SIMD distance, and ACID-transactional index updates
- **Blob storage** -- content-addressed dedup, chunked writes, causal lineage graph
- **TTL tables** -- per-key expiration for sessions, caches, and ephemeral agent state
- **CDC** -- row-level change capture for replication and reactive pipelines
- **Composite queries** -- ranked fusion across semantic, temporal, and causal signals
- **Runs anywhere** -- `no_std` core compiles to wasm32, ARM Cortex, RISC-V. No allocator, no filesystem required

One binary. One file. ACID crash-safe.

> **Single-process recommended.** shodh-redb uses `try_lock`/`try_lock_shared` to prevent the
> same process from opening a database twice (returns `DatabaseAlreadyOpen`). However, on
> platforms where file locks are unsupported (e.g., some network filesystems), the lock is
> silently skipped. Multi-process access to the same file is not supported and will corrupt data.

## Quick start

```rust
use shodh_redb::{Database, TableDefinition, ReadableDatabase, ReadableTable};

const TABLE: TableDefinition<&str, u64> = TableDefinition::new("agent_state");

let db = Database::create("agent.redb")?;

let wtxn = db.begin_write()?;
{
    let mut table = wtxn.open_table(TABLE)?;
    table.insert("task_count", &42u64)?;
}
wtxn.commit()?;

let rtxn = db.begin_read()?;
let table = rtxn.open_table(TABLE)?;
assert_eq!(table.get("task_count")?.unwrap().value(), 42);
```

## Vector search

Native IVF-PQ index with integer ADC, residual encoding, and per-vector metadata filtering.

```rust
use shodh_redb::{FixedVec, DistanceMetric, nearest_k, TableDefinition};

// Brute-force top-k (small datasets)
const EMBEDDINGS: TableDefinition<u64, FixedVec<384>> = TableDefinition::new("memory");
let results = nearest_k(
    table.iter()?.map(|r| { let (k, v) = r.unwrap(); (k.value(), v.value().to_vec()) }),
    &query, 10, |a, b| DistanceMetric::Cosine.compute(a, b),
);
```

Three quantization levels:

| Type | Compression | Distance |
|---|---|---|
| `FixedVec<N>` / `DynVec` | None (f32) | Cosine, L2, dot, Manhattan |
| `ScalarQuantized<N>` | ~4x (u8) | Approximate L2 |
| `BinaryQuantized<N>` | 32x (1-bit) | Hamming |

For datasets beyond brute-force range, use the **IVF-PQ index** -- inverted file with product quantization, integer asymmetric distance tables, and optional reranking from stored raw vectors.

### Blob store

Content-addressed storage with SHA-256 dedup, chunked streaming writes, and causal lineage tracking.

```rust
let blob_id = wtxn.store_blob(data, ContentType::ImagePng, "screenshot", &opts)?;
let reader = rtxn.blob_reader(blob_id)?;
```

Per-blob tags, namespaces, temporal indexing, and causal graph with BFS traversal.

### TTL tables

Per-key expiration. Lazy filtering on read, bulk purge on demand.

```rust
let mut table = wtxn.open_table(CACHE)?;
table.insert_with_ttl(&"result_abc", data, Duration::from_secs(1800))?;
table.purge_expired()?;
```

### Merge operators

Atomic read-modify-write without manual locking.

```rust
table.merge(&"tool_calls", &1u64.to_le_bytes(), &NumericAdd)?;
```

Built-in: `NumericAdd`, `SaturatingAdd`, `FloatAdd`, `NumericMax`, `NumericMin`, `BitwiseOr`, `BytesAppend`. Implement `MergeOperator` for custom logic.

### CDC (change data capture)

Row-level change streaming with cursors, retention pruning, and HLC timestamps.

### Composite queries

Multi-signal ranked retrieval fusing semantic similarity, temporal recency, causal proximity, and namespace/tag filtering into a single scored result set.

### Multimap tables

Multiple values per key for tag indices, inverted lookups, and many-to-many relationships.

### Group commit

Batched fsync for write-heavy workloads. Multiple operations share a single transaction and disk sync.

### SIMD vector ops

Distance functions use hand-written AVX2 intrinsics on x86_64 with runtime feature detection and scalar fallback.

| Function | dim=128 | dim=384 | dim=1536 | Peak throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `dot_product` | 6.2 ns | 17.8 ns | 75.8 ns | 173 GB/s |
| `euclidean_distance_sq` | 9.6 ns | 23.8 ns | 92.5 ns | 133 GB/s |
| `cosine_similarity` | 13.7 ns | 34.6 ns | 124.8 ns | 99 GB/s |
| `manhattan_distance` | 7.3 ns | 21.2 ns | 102.1 ns | 145 GB/s |
| `hamming_distance` | 18.5 ns | 12.5 ns | -- | 62 GB/s |

| Function | Strategy |
|---|---|
| `dot_product` | `_mm256_mul_ps` + `_mm256_add_ps`, 8 f32/iter |
| `euclidean_distance_sq` | Fused sub+mul, 8 f32/iter |
| `cosine_similarity` | 3 accumulators, 8 f32/iter |
| `manhattan_distance` | `_mm256_andnot_ps` for abs |
| `hamming_distance` | Mula's vectorized popcount (`pshufb` + SAD), 32 bytes/iter |

On `no_std` or non-x86 targets, scalar code is structured for LLVM auto-vectorization.

### Zero-copy serialization

On little-endian targets (x86, ARM LE, RISC-V LE), `FixedVec` and `DynVec` use bulk `copy_nonoverlapping` -- the f32 memory layout matches the on-disk LE format directly.

## `no_std` support

The core library compiles with `#![no_std]` (disable the `std` feature). Vector types, distance functions, quantization, IVF-PQ indexing, and the B-tree engine all work without the standard library. Targets: wasm32, ARM Cortex-M, RISC-V bare metal.

The `std` feature adds file backends, TTL tables, group commit, and runtime SIMD dispatch. A flash translation layer (FTL) backend supports raw NOR/NAND flash on embedded targets without a filesystem.

---

## Compression

Value-level compression is built in via two algorithms, off by default and selected per database:

| Algorithm | Cargo feature | Crate | When to use |
|---|---|---|---|
| LZ4 | `compression_lz4` | [`lz4_flex`](https://crates.io/crates/lz4_flex) | Latency-sensitive workloads -- LZ4 prioritizes decompression speed over ratio |
| zstd | `compression_zstd` | [`zstd`](https://crates.io/crates/zstd) | Storage-bound or cold data -- better compression ratio at higher CPU cost (level 1-22, default 3) |
| Both | `compression` | -- | Build with both available, choose at database open time |

```toml
[dependencies]
shodh-redb = { version = "0.4", features = ["compression_lz4"] }
# or: features = ["compression_zstd"]
# or: features = ["compression"]    # both
```

**Why off by default:**
- `no_std` / embedded targets (Cortex-M, wasm32) often cannot pull in `zstd`
- Adds CPU on every value insert and read; not always a win
- Smaller default dependency tree, faster compile, smaller attack surface

Compression operates at the value level: each value is compressed *before* entering the B-tree, with a self-describing 5-byte envelope (1-byte flags + 4-byte original size). Values that don't shrink are stored raw with zero envelope overhead. The chosen algorithm is recorded in the database header and validated on open -- a database written with `compression_zstd` will refuse to open without that feature.

# Fuzz regression corpus

Inputs that once crashed or hung a fuzz target, kept so they are replayed
forever. Two purposes:

1. **Regression coverage.** A fixed bug stays fixed. Fuzzing is probabilistic --
   rediscovering a given input is not guaranteed, so a fix verified only by "the
   fuzzer stopped complaining" is not verified at all.
2. **Diagnosis.** The `Fuzz Regressions` workflow replays these under
   AddressSanitizer, which prints a stack trace for a hang or crash. That is the
   only way to get one here: cargo-fuzz cannot link on Windows MSVC, because
   `__start___sancov_cntrs` and friends are ELF section-boundary symbols that
   the COFF linker does not synthesise. Fuzzing is Linux/macOS only.

## Layout

    fuzz/regressions/<target-name>/<artifact-file>

The file name is cargo-fuzz's own (`crash-<sha1>`, `timeout-<sha1>`), so it can
be traced back to the run that produced it. Contents are the raw input bytes.

## Adding one

When CI reports a fuzz failure, download the artifact from the run (PR CI and
the nightly both upload them now) and drop it in the matching directory. If the
artifact was lost, the input can be reconstructed from the `Base64:` line that
libFuzzer prints in the log.
